rules.sentence: The criterion defining the presence of dementia is memory compromise in at least two domains which is sufficient to interfere in activities of daily living.
Cerebrovascular Disease (CVD) is determined by focal neurological signs of CVD on the exam, in addition to positive evidence of CVD on tomography or resonance imaging.
Finally, the NINDS-AIREN deems the onset of dementia as within three months of a stroke (CVA) with abrupt deterioration of cognitive functions and a course which fluctuates in a step-wise fashion.
In order to reach an accurate diagnosis, screening must be carried out which evaluates risk factors, manifestation of a cerebrovascular episode and the occurrence of the dementia picture
Engel et al. (2003) consider risk factors of dementia to be Systemic Arterial Hypertension (SAH), smoking, diabetes, alcoholism, heart disease, atherosclerosis, dyslipidemia and obesity.
Other risk factors associated to VaD are black race, low schooling and male gender.
Identifying these risk factors, as well as diagnosing early VaD, allows preventive strategies to be devised which may improve the evolution of the patient or prevent the onset of the disease.
